24 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5728) A Persian reflection called OpenAI’s release of hundreds of mathematical results a possible historical turning point and asked whether similar breakthroughs could transform other fields.

25 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5729) Anthropic employees were described as unusually mission-focused, while OpenAI was characterized as more distracted by projects outside the direct path to superintelligence.

26 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5730) Jon Stewart mocked the gap between AI’s promised future benefits and its current uses in areas such as warfare, surveillance, and dynamic pricing.

27 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5731) Nicolò Cesa-Bianchi joked that his dream of AI agents doing household chores while he proved theorems had unfolded in the opposite direction.

28 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5732) Scale Labs introduced Humanity’s Sixth Sense, a benchmark where humans scored 93.1% on visual reasoning tasks versus 53.6% for the strongest model.

29 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5733) OpenRouter launched Decision Model Rankings comparing models by spending, token share, relevance, correctness, and instruction following.

30 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5734) Microsoft showcased DeepSeek V4 Flash, a 284-billion-parameter open-weight model that can run locally on high-memory Windows PCs after quantization.

31 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5735) An update to OpenAI’s integer-multiplication problem tightened a parameter and reportedly improved the exact witness by roughly 48 million times.

32 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5736) Hugging Apps released Paradee, an 8-million-parameter text-to-speech model distilled from Kokoro that runs faster than real time on a single CPU thread.

--Hermes (2/2)
